title: Conflicting Information Across Timeframes
hook: The higher timeframe provides context, but lower-timeframe structure shows what price is doing right now. Learn which question each timeframe is answering.

launchpad.outcome: Tell a lower-timeframe correction apart from a broader structural shift, and explain why waiting is sometimes correct.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Which question is each timeframe answering?

slides.headline: When timeframes disagree, ask which question each one answers.
slides.line: The higher timeframe provides context, but lower-timeframe structure shows what price is doing right now.

slides.headline: Timeframes disagree because each one shows a different view.
slides.line: A bearish move on a lower timeframe may be a correction inside a larger bullish structure.

steps.text: On the bigger view, price is making higher highs and higher lows. The structure is bullish.
Zoom in on the pullback. On a lower timeframe it shows lower highs and lower lows, which is bearish.
Both views are true. The bearish move may be a correction within the larger bullish structure.

slides.headline: Each timeframe answers a different question.
slides.line: Tap each one. When timeframes disagree, ask which question each one is answering.

steps.label: 15M (15-minute)
steps.sub: What is developing near those levels? Recommended for extra confluence, not required.

slides.headline: Is a bearish 1H a correction or a real change?
slides.line: When the 4H is bullish and the 1H turns bearish, it can be a developing correction or evidence of a larger structural change.

cards.label: Developing correction
cards.sub: The 1H is pulling back, but the 4H higher lows still hold.

cards.label: Larger structural change
cards.sub: The 4H structure itself changes, for example a higher low breaks.

check.prompt: The 4H is bullish. The 1H is making lower highs, but the 4H higher low is holding. What can you say so far?

options.label: It may be a developing correction inside the bullish 4H
options.why: Right. The larger structure has not broken, so the 1H move can still be a correction.

options.label: The 4H trend is over, so look for shorts
options.feedback: Nothing on the 4H has broken yet. A bearish 1H on its own does not prove the larger structure changed.

slides.headline: Let a bullish 1H shift confirm before you reconsider longs.
slides.line: When the overall market thesis is bullish but the 4H has developed bearish structure, wait for a bullish 1H market structure shift (MSS) before reconsidering long entries.

steps.text: The 4H has developed bearish structure. On the 1H, price is making lower highs and lower lows.
Mark the last 1H lower high. Until price closes above it, there is no bullish shift, so you wait.
Price closes above that lower high. That is a bullish 1H MSS, so you can reconsider longs, and the 1M still has to earn the entry.

slides.headline: The 4H and 1H are bullish, but the 15M is pulling back.
slides.line: Before you decide the lower-timeframe move is ending, observe where it is happening and what the 15M structure does.

steps.text: The 4H and 1H are bullish, but the 15M is making lower highs and lower lows for now.
First observe where the pullback is happening. Is it reaching a level the 1H says matters?
Then watch the 15M structure. Until it closes above its last lower high, the pullback has not shown that it is ending.

check.prompt: The 4H and 1H are bullish. The 15M is still making lower lows at the 1H level. Has the pullback ended?

options.label: Yes, it reached the 1H level
options.feedback: Reaching a level is something to observe, not proof. The 15M is still making lower lows, so the pullback has not shown it is ending.

options.label: Not yet, the 15M structure has not shifted
options.why: Right. You keep observing until the 15M structure shows the pullback is ending.

slides.headline: Recognizing the pattern is not the same as qualifying the trade.
slides.line: The 1M can complete a clean bullish ICC even when the higher-timeframe structure does not support a long.

versus.label: Qualifying the trade
points: The 4H and 1H structure support a long.

check.prompt: A clean bullish 1M ICC completes, but the 4H and 1H structure do not support a long. Do you take it?

options.label: Yes, the 1M model completed
options.feedback: The 1M only answers whether the entry model completed. The higher timeframes still have to support the direction.

options.label: No, the pattern is there but the trade does not qualify
options.why: Exactly. You recognized the pattern, and you also saw that the environment does not support the long.

slides.headline: Sometimes the best decision is to stand aside.
slides.line: Tap each card. When any of these is true, you wait instead of forcing a direction.

cards.label: Structure is unclear
cards.sub: You cannot tell which way the swings are building.

cards.label: Timeframes contradict
cards.sub: They give opposite answers, and nothing has confirmed either one.

cards.label: Plan conditions are not met
cards.sub: What your plan requires is not there yet, so there is no trade.

slides.headline: When new structure develops, reassess your read.
slides.line: Waiting does not last forever. New structure gives you new information, so you look again.

cards.label: A new swing forms
cards.sub: It may become the more relevant structural reference.

cards.label: A structural break
cards.sub: A key swing breaks, so the old read may no longer fit.

cards.label: An MSS changes the thesis
cards.sub: A market structure shift can change the direction you are looking for.

slides.title: Read what each timeframe is telling you.
slides.say: Read all three charts. Then decide if there is enough confirmation to keep going.

asks.prompt: What are the three timeframes communicating?

options.label: All three are bullish and aligned
options.why: Right. The 4H environment, the 1H structure and the 15M are all pointing up.

options.label: The 15M disagrees with the 4H
options.feedback: Look at the 15M again. It is making higher highs and higher lows, just like the 4H and 1H.

asks.prompt: Is there enough confirmation to keep following your bullish plan?

options.label: Yes, and the 1M entry model still has to complete
options.why: Yes. The context supports a long, and the 1M still has to answer whether your entry model completed.

options.label: Yes, so buy right now
options.feedback: Aligned context is not an entry. The 1M still has to answer whether your entry model completed.

options.label: No, everything is too unclear
options.feedback: All three timeframes agree here. This is the clearest picture you can get.

slides.outro: ALIGNED ✓ Every timeframe agrees. Now the 1M has to earn the entry.

slides.title: The higher timeframes agree, but the 15M does not.

b.label: 1H
b.note: Bullish, pulling back to a level

slides.say: Read all three charts. What is the 15M telling you, and is it finished?

options.label: A temporary pullback inside the bullish 4H and 1H
options.why: Right. The 15M is countertrend for now, while the larger structure is still bullish.

options.label: The bullish structure has ended
options.feedback: The 4H and 1H have not broken. A bearish 15M on its own does not change the larger structure.

asks.prompt: Is there enough confirmation to say the pullback is over?

options.label: Not yet, the 15M is still making lower lows
options.why: Right. Keep observing the 15M near the 1H level before you conclude the pullback is ending.

options.label: Yes, the 4H and 1H are bullish
options.feedback: The higher timeframes give context. They do not tell you the 15M pullback has finished.

slides.outro: OBSERVE ✓ The bigger picture is bullish, and the 15M pullback has not shown that it is ending yet.

slides.title: Your thesis is bullish, but the 4H and 1H disagree.

a.label: 4H
a.note: A lower high, then a lower low

b.label: 1H
b.note: Bouncing, but below its last lower high

slides.say: Your overall thesis is bullish. Read the 4H and the 1H, then decide.

options.label: The 4H turned bearish, and the 1H is only bouncing
options.why: Right. The 4H made a lower high and a lower low, and the 1H has not shifted yet.

options.label: Both are bullish again
options.feedback: The 4H broke its higher low and made a lower low. That is bearish structure, not bullish.

asks.prompt: Is there enough confirmation to look for long entries?

options.label: Yes, the overall thesis is bullish
options.feedback: The thesis alone is not enough. The 4H has developed bearish structure, so structure has to confirm first.

options.label: Yes, the 1H bounce is enough
options.feedback: A bounce is not a shift. The 1H has not closed above its last lower high yet.

options.label: No, wait for a bullish 1H market structure shift
options.why: Exactly. When the 4H has developed bearish structure against a bullish thesis, you wait for a bullish 1H MSS before reconsidering longs.

slides.outro: WAIT ✓ The 4H and 1H disagree and nothing has confirmed. Standing aside is the decision.

slides.quote: The higher timeframe provides context. Lower-timeframe structure shows what price is doing right now.

slides.prompt: In your own words, why is waiting sometimes the right call when timeframes disagree?
slides.modelAnswer: Each timeframe answers a different question. A lower-timeframe move against the 4H can be a correction or the start of a larger structural change, and until structure confirms which one it is, I don’t force a direction. If my thesis is bullish but the 4H has developed bearish structure, I wait for a bullish 1H market structure shift before reconsidering longs.

takeaways: Each timeframe answers a different question, so disagreement is normal.
A lower-timeframe move against the 4H may be a correction, not a structural change.
If the 4H turns bearish against a bullish thesis, wait for a bullish 1H MSS before reconsidering longs.
A completed 1M pattern only qualifies when the higher-timeframe structure supports it.
remember: WHEN TIMEFRAMES DISAGREE, LET STRUCTURE CONFIRM BEFORE YOU ACT.
